On the track, Halsey thows jabs at her ex-boyfriend and rapper, G-Eazy, and calls out his infidelity.

Following her tumultuous on-and-off relationship with G-Eazy, Halsey penned her hit October 2018 single “Without Me.” In a June 2019 Rolling Stone interview she claimed:

he cheated on [me] in front of the entire world, like, a billion times.

According to a June 2018 Daily Star article, during their time together, G-Eazy sent several sexts to an unknown woman in November 2017.

On February 9, 2019, Halsey hosted Saturday Night Live, performing a piano version of “Without Me.” During the performance, the background lit up to reveal walls covered with hand-painted notes, some of which saying:

Ashley I cheated
At home in Los Angeles
In Minneapolis

In these lines, Halsey alludes to her bisexuality, implying that instead of turning against the other women in the situation, she joined forces to get back at G-Eazy.

“Tracks” is slang for a type of hair extensions because the pattern at the base of the extension can resemble train tracks.

“No más” is Spanish for “no more” and, considering the previous line, seems to imply the girl 21 is having sex with is experiencing some level of discomfort. Additionally, “hit her from the back” could be indicative of anal sex, which is often painful for the female partner.

It might also be a reference to the shocking conclusion of the famous bout between Sugar Ray Leonard and Roberto Durán, where Durán suddenly quit the fight in the midway through the eighth round by raising his hand and saying “No más” to the referee.

line: I ain’t with the cakin’, how you kiss that? (Kiss that)
vault_lines: I ain't with the cakin', how you kiss that? (Kiss that)
meaning:
“Caking” means to spend time with a love interest and build a relationship. 21 isn’t looking for love; he just wants sex.

Post first teased “rockstar” in December 2016, so 21 likely wrote this verse long prior to the song’s release. But since then he’s switched it up and gone the romance route—in July 2017, rumors started surfacing that he was in a serious relationship with model and actress Amber Rose. They even met each other’s parents.

Alternatively, 21 might be insinuating that he doesn’t like women who cake their face in make-up, asking “how you kiss that” to imply that while others might do so, he personally couldn’t bring himself to kiss someone who is “caked” in make-up.

line: Cocaine on the table, liquor pourin’, don’t give a damn
vault_lines: Cocaine on the table, liquor pourin', don't give a damn
meaning: Drugs, alcohol, and rock music have always been intertwined, often to tragic effect. Brian Jones' drug and alcohol abuse led him to drown in his pool in 1969, Bon Scott, who Post name-dropped at the beginning of the verse, died of alcohol poisoning in 1980, and Janis Joplin, Jimi Hendrix, and Jim Morrison all died of drug overdoses at just 27 years old. Post is embracing this “live fast, die young” rockstar lifestyle.

line: Shit was legendary Threw a TV out the window of the Montage
vault_lines: Threw a TV out the window of the Montage
meaning:
The Montage is a chain of five-star luxury hotels. Post’s friend and collaborator Justin Bieber has reportedly lived at the Beverly Hills location since late 2016.

Trashing hotel rooms—and specifically tossing TVs out of hotel windows—is a rockstar tradition. Although there’s no consensus about who started the trend, some believe the inciting event was when The Rolling Stones guitarist Keith Richards and keyboardist Bobby Keys launched their TV off of a West Hollywood hotel balcony in 1972.

line: Sweeter than a Pop-Tart, you know you are not hard
vault_lines: Sweeter than a Pop-Tart, you know you are not hard
meaning:
A Pop-Tart is a pre-baked toaster pastry that’s hard on the outside but soft and gooey on the inside.

“Hard” is a street term for being tough. By saying “you are not hard”, 21 is saying this person isn’t tough enough for the streets. He compares them to a Pop-Tart, as they act hard on the outside but on the inside, they’re too soft and sweet, unlike the image they are trying to set for themselves.



Mos Def and Talib Kweli used similar euphemisms on “Re:Definition” talking about people being sweet enough to cause cavities and “sweeter than some cinnamon” and not tough.

Finally, Pop-tart is also a reference to a “pop star” which has considerably less authenticity/hardness than a true rapper.

line: Close that door, we blowin’ smoke She ask me light a fire like I’m Morrison (Ayy) Act a fool on stage Prolly leave my fuckin’ show in a cop car (Ayy)
vault_lines: Close that door, we blowin' smoke
meaning:
“Light My Fire,” released in 1967, is one of The Doors' biggest hits. That year, it topped the Billboard Hot 100 list for three weeks and was certified Gold by the RIAA.

On December 9, 1967, the band’s frontman Jim Morrison was arrested during a live show in New Haven, Connecticut following an incident where he was insubordinate to a police officer backstage. The crowd rioted, and Morrison became the first ever rockstar taken into custody during a performance.



Three years later, Morrison was arrested on stage again, this time in Miami, Florida for exposing his genitals to the crowd and feigning masturbation.

Post sports the faces of music legends tattooed on his fingers. In a 2016 GQ interview, after he talked about adding Jim Morrison to one of his digits, he said “without these guys, I wouldn’t be making music right now.”

line: Fuckin’ with me, call up on a Uzi And show up, man, them the shottas When my homies pull up on your block They make that thing go grra-ta-ta-ta (Pow, pow, pow, ayy, ayy)
vault_lines: When my homies pull up on your block
meaning:
“Shottas” are loyal gangsters who you can call upon to commit violence or murders. The term was popularized by the 2002 Jamaican movie of the same name, which is a drama about two young men involved in organized crime in Kingston, Jamaica and Miami, Florida. Loyalty is one of the film’s key themes.

“Gra-ta-ta-ta” is an onomatopoeia for a gunshot.

Hollywood Hills is an upscale neighborhood located deep in the Santa Monica Mountains. This area hosts high-end homes and celebrities like Justin Timberlake, Dr. Dre, and Big Sean.

It’s no stretch of the imagination that 21 is big enough to be a pop star since he achieved major mainstream success. On his July 2017 hit “Bank Account,” he bragged about having eight million dollars to his name, and buying a house in the Hills:

Straight up out the 6, now got a house in the Hills, dog

line: All my brothers got that gas And they always be smokin’ like a Rasta
vault_lines: All my brothers got that gas
meaning: A Rasta is a follower of the Rastafari religion, a Jamaican movement that saw its first major rise in popularity in the 1930s. One of the most iconic Rastas was Bob Marley, who popularized the faith with his music in the ‘70s. Rastas are known for sporting dreadlocks and smoking marijuana, which “gas” is slang for. Smoking ganja is a sacramental component of the Rastafarian religion.

line: I done made the hot chart, ’member I used to trap hard
vault_lines: I done made the hot chart, 'member I used to trap hard
meaning:
21 used to be a drug dealer and was involved in gang violence. However, the arrival of his debut album Issa in July 2017 earned him hits like “Bank Account” which peaked at #12 on the Billboard Hot 100 list.

Even before that, his tracks “X” and “No Heart” both cracked the top 50 on Billboard, and through his Drake collaboration “Sneakin'”, he cracked the top 25. His first song to chart as a solo artist was “Red Opps” which peaked at 74 in 2015.

line: I’ve been fuckin’ hoes and poppin’ pillies Man, I feel just like a rockstar (Ayy, ayy)
vault_lines: I've been fuckin' hoes and poppin' pillies
meaning:
Post is putting his own spin on “sex, drugs, and rock and roll,” a pop culture catchphrase that characterizes the rockstar lifestyle. The saying actually derives from Ian Dury’s 1977 song “Sex & Drugs & Rock & Roll.” Even though it didn’t chart well, it slowly became an anthem because of Dury’s electric live performances.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=erGNSQMJ79Q

It’s no surprise that Post would evoke the phrase, since his influences span all genres, and he’s even recorded straight-up rock and country songs like “Feeling Whitney” from his 2016 album Stoney.

line: Dude, your girlfriend is a groupie, she just tryna get in Sayin’, ”I’m with the band”, ayy, ayy Now she actin’ outta pocket, tryna grab up on my pants Hundred bitches in my trailer say they ain’t got a man And they all brought a friend, yeah, ayy
vault_lines: Dude, your girlfriend is a groupie, she just tryna get in
meaning:
“I’m with the band” is a phrase groupies use to get past security. It’s so ubiquitous that one of rock’s most notorious groupies, Pamela Des Barres, named her 1987 tell-all memoir after it.

In the book, she recounted her drug-fueled sexual escapades in the 1960s rock world, including her affairs with rockstars like Keith Moon of The Who, Jimmy Page of Led Zeppelin, and Mick Jagger of The Rolling Stones. Des Barres' story epitomized the stereotypical groupie lifestyle that Post describes here.

line: Switch my whip, came back in black I’m startin’ sayin’, “Rest in peace to Bon Scott” (Ayy)
vault_lines: Switch my whip, came back in black
meaning: On 19 February 1980, Bon Scott, the lead singer of the rock band AC/DC, drank himself to death at the age of 33. Scott and the band were working on Back in Black at the time—although they briefly considered calling it quits after he passed, they ended up releasing the album as a tribute to him, and it became their best-selling and most critically acclaimed endeavor.
